items.title: GigaChat 4 opens weights: 708B total, 41B active
items.summary: ai-sage released GigaChat 4 on Hugging Face, a flagship model that combines MoE with DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) and Gated DeltaNet (GDN), with 708B total parameters and 41B active per token, a one-million-token context window, and instant and reasoning modes in a single model selectable per request; a 37B (4B active) size is also available. The 708B model ships under the MIT License, giving teams another open option for long-context, multilingual and agentic work.

evidence.quote: GigaChat 4 is the flagship hybrid model of the GigaChat family. It combines a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture with DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) and Gated DeltaNet (GDN) with 708B total parameters and 41B active parameters per token.
GigaChat 4 supports both modes within a single model, selectable per request. It features a one-million-token context window
GigaChat 4 is a family of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models available in two sizes: 708B (41B active) and 37B (4B active) parameters.
GigaChat 4 is released under the MIT License

items.title: Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX over Grok's sexualized images
items.summary: Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones sued SpaceX, the parent of X, xAI and Grok, and Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield filed a separate but similar action, alleging Grok created CSAM and non-consensual intimate images while the company publicly assured consumers that robust protections were in place. For teams shipping image and video generation, it turns the question of whether advertised safeguards actually work into a legal one.

evidence.quote: Today’s suit was filed in collaboration with Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield, who filed a separate but similar action.
its subsidiaries publicly assured consumers that robust protections were in place to prevent Grok from creating CSAM, NCII, and other sexualized images.

items.title: Kimi launches Kimi for Science with API credits for researchers
items.summary: Kimi's new Kimi for Science program offers selected researchers up to $20,000 in Kimi API credits (approx. 7B tokens), plus technical support and early access to new models; the first cohort applies by Dec 8. Research teams using LLMs for literature review or data analysis can apply, though the credits are for model usage, not cash funding.

evidence.quote: Selected applicants will receive up to $20,000 in Kimi API credits (approx. 7B tokens), with the exact amount determined by research needs and review outcomes.

items.title: inclusionAI open-sources design model Ming-Image-0.2-Design
items.summary: inclusionAI released Ming-Image-0.2-Design, a 6B (DiT) visual-design generation model under the MIT License that improves complex composition, lighting and text rendering for e-commerce hero images, UI design drafts and spatial renderings. The card lists it #1 among open-weight models overall on AA-Image-T2I v2.1 as of Nov 25, 2026, making it worth a try when you need an open model that renders text.

evidence.quote: The new version improves complex composition, lighting, and text rendering, and can be used to create e-commerce hero images, UI design drafts, and spatial renderings.

items.title: MemTensor releases memory foundation model MemT-1.0-Pro
items.summary: MemTensor released MemT-1.0-Pro, built on NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B with 554B total and 59B activated parameters plus 4.23B trainable memory parameters, making persistent memory part of model computation so it needn't access the original context at inference. MemTensor says its state cuts storage by approximately 66× versus a full-context KV cache at 128K history, relevant to agent builders watching long-session costs.

evidence.quote: MemT-1.0 is a new generation of memory foundation models that makes persistent, dynamically evolving memory an intrinsic part of model computation.
Its persistent state remains constant in size, reducing storage by approximately 66× versus full-context KV cache at 128K history length.

items.title: OS-Omni benchmarks computer-use agents across desktop, mobile and web
items.summary: OS-Omni is a live benchmark spanning Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android and Web; human studies show its tasks need 67.54 interaction steps versus 15.0 for OSWorld. The strongest agent, Claude Opus 5.5, reaches 68.5% average success, 8.8 points behind the 77.3% human reference, so it is a useful test for long-horizon, cross-device agents.

evidence.quote: Human studies show that OS-Omni tasks require 67.54 interaction steps, substantially exceeding OSWorld references of 15.0 steps. On v1, the strongest evaluated agent, Claude Opus 5.5, reaches 68.5% average success, trailing the 77.3% human reference by 8.8 points

items.title: Stable GDN-2 fixes Gated DeltaNet-2 long-context training failures
items.summary: The paper traces Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) long-context training failures to asymmetric erasure and proposes Stable GDN-2, using symmetric erasure and decay-regulated residual writing. On ~1.6B parameter models it trains stably and boosts the 128K average RULER score by 6.80 points in the recurrent setting, a worthwhile read for anyone building linear-attention long-sequence models.

evidence.quote: To resolve this, we propose Stable GDN-2, employing symmetric erasure to ensure non-expansive state propagation and decay-regulated residual writing to preserve writing flexibility.

Experiments on ~1.6B parameter models show that Stable GDN-2 achieves stable training alongside improved long-context retrieval. Compared to GDN-2, it boosts the 128K average RULER score by 6.80 points in the recurrent setting

items.title: Coding agents beat video models at visual reasoning
items.summary: Given the same tasks, inputs and evaluator, a coding agent writes a program that renders the answer video instead of denoising pixels. On VBVR-Pro-Bench, Codex, Claude Code and Gemini CLI score 0.923, 0.894 and 0.893, more than 0.22 above the strongest video model, suggesting program synthesis is currently the more reliable route for such tasks.

evidence.quote: On VBVR-Pro-Bench, Codex, Claude Code and Gemini CLI score 0.92 / 0.89 / 0.89, more than 0.22 above the strongest video model.

items.title: DRBench Pro scores deep research agents on knowledge coverage
items.summary: DRBench Pro builds knowledge trees from Wikipedia to generate research queries and evidence-grounded rubrics, measuring breadth and depth of coverage across 144 research cases, 24 domains and 44,102 rubrics. The best-performing agent reaches 57.04% overall coverage, giving research-agent teams a way to find gaps in breadth versus depth.

evidence.quote: DRBench Pro includes 144 research cases across 24 domains and 44,102 rubrics

items.title: Hugging Face generates sound-on video with LTX-2.5 on Trainium3
items.summary: A Hugging Face blog post runs Lightricks' LTX-2.5 via diffusers on AWS Trainium3, chaining shots from a JSON film file; once models are loaded, a 10-second 2048×1024 clip with sound takes 22 to 23 s on half of the machine, rivaling LTX's API. The code is in dacorvo/video-generation, a useful reference for deploying video generation on Trainium.

evidence.quote: I picked LTX-2.5 from Lightricks, which generates video and sound together. By the end, once the models were loaded, a 10-second clip with sound took 22 to 23 s to generate, on half of the machine.
